title: ScreenConnect remote session actions
volume: None on a normal day for the account rule. The file rule makes one detection for each program a technician pushes, a few a day where installers go out through ScreenConnect.
mdr_note: These detections are yours to work. Sophos MDR doesn't work custom detections, and a case your own case rule opens from them is Managed By Self.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: Two custom detection rules for ConnectWise ScreenConnect, on the ManagementEvent records the library's ScreenConnect parsers write from its session automation. They make a detection when a command queued through a session adds a local account or a local group member, and when a session sends a program or script to a machine. Each rule matches sensor type ConnectWise ScreenConnect only.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the library's ScreenConnect parsers and send the automations in its README through bridges/webhook-relay, which adds the HTTP Ingest key, then run the check-your-data search to see events arrive.
- The session automation's event filter needs QueuedCommand and SentFiles.

How it works:
- The parsers write a queued command's text as the command and a sent file's name as the result, with the guest machine as the target host.
- The account rule takes queued commands with net user, net1 user or net localgroup and /add, New-LocalUser or Add-LocalGroupMember, in any case.
- The file rule takes sent files whose names hold one of nine program and script extensions.

Tuning:
- If technicians push one installer to every machine, leave it out in the query itself, such as and result !contains 'AgentSetup.exe'. A suppression rule would hide Sophos's detections for those machines as well.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-23, each query returned exactly the sample lines tests.json lists in Data Lake Search, and the rules run offline on the same 3 records agreed. The samples went in with their dates moved to the day before the test, so they fell inside the search's time range.
- As live rules there, each one fired on exactly its sample lines. Lines sent in the first 12 minutes after the rules were made made no detection on either rule; sent again about 30 minutes after, they did.
- No Sophos detector made a detection on the lines these rules take. Sophos's sign-in analytics flagged only a sample sign-in on Auth, as an unseen user, address or application.
- The lines went through bridges/webhook-relay, run on the lab machine, as text/plain, the way ScreenConnect's Perform Web Request sends them.

Known gaps:
- A command typed into a remote shell on the machine isn't a ScreenConnect command event. Sophos's own detections on the machine cover what it runs.
- A file sent inside an archive, or renamed to another extension, makes none.
